item.research_question: How does the addition of Sn (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) affect the phase constitution, microstructure, and magnetic properties (specifically saturation magnetization, remanence, and Curie temperature) of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc-melting of 99.99% purity constituent elements using a water-cooled Cu crucible, followed by suction casting into a 100 × 10× 2 mm water-cooled Cu mold after remelting four times.
item.test_conditions: XRD scan speed of 1°/min; VSM measurements at an applied magnetic field of 1 T; HCTS hysteresis curves using a 27 × 9 × 1.7 mm rectangular sample at a magnetic field of 25 kA/m; DSC thermal stability analysis at a heating rate of 10 K/min.
key_findings: The ratio of I(110)BCC/I(111)FCC increases from 0.38 (x=0) to 10.53 (x=0.10), indicating a rapid increase in BCC phase content.
Saturation magnetization (Ms) increases from 78.6 Am2/kg to 88.8 Am2/kg as x increases from 0 to 0.10, an increase of almost 13 percent.
The Curie temperature of the FCC phase increases significantly, reaching 634.9 K for x = 0.04.
Remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn, which is different from the effect of Ga addition.
The average size of nanoscale precipitates in the BCC matrix changes from 20 ± 5 nm (rod-like) in the Sn-free alloy to approximately 100 nm length and 30 nm width in the x=0.10 alloy.
A phase transformation from FCC to BCC occurs at temperatures between 600–700 K, causing magnetization to increase in this range.
Unknown phases appear in XRD patterns for x ≥ 0.02, which are inferred to be rich in Cu, Ni, and Sn.
item.mechanism: The addition of Sn promotes the formation of the BCC phase, which has a higher Curie temperature and higher saturation magnetization than the FCC phase. The increase in magnetization at high temperatures (600–700 K) is attributed to the transformation of the FCC phase (low Tc) to the BCC phase (high Tc). The shape change of Cu-rich nano-precipitates is due to the segregation of Cu and Sn in the phase boundary regions and the decrease of Cu solubility in the BCC phase.
item.limitations: The text notes that for x ≥ 0.08, only a small number of FCC phase transform to BCC phase, limiting the magnetization increase at higher temperatures. Additionally, unknown phases appear in the XRD patterns for x ≥ 0.02, the composition of which is only partially deduced.
item.future_work: The authors propose that these alloys can be used as new soft magnetic materials at high temperatures and suggest the work provides a new idea for designing future high-performance soft magnetic materials.
quotes: The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix.
The phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K.
The value of Ms increases from 78.6 Am2/kg to 88.8 Am2/kg as x increases from 0 to 0.10, which increases almost 13 percent.
